entries.name: Actual Budget
entries.summary: Budget by envelopes, with your accounts kept on your own server.
entries.description:
Actual Budget is a personal finance app built around envelope budgeting: the
money you earn is each given a job. It syncs between your devices through
this server and can import from YNAB, QIF, OFX and CSV files. The first visit
sets the server's password.

entries.name: AdGuard Home
entries.summary: Block ads and trackers for every device on your network.
entries.description:
A network-wide ad and tracker blocker that works as your home DNS server.
Because other devices depend on it, this Node keeps a fixed address and
starts AdGuard Home before anything else.

entries.name: Audiobookshelf
entries.summary: Your audiobooks and podcasts, streamed to every device, each listener's place kept.
entries.description:
Audiobookshelf serves your audiobooks and podcasts to its phone apps and any browser.
It fetches covers and chapters, downloads new podcast episodes, and keeps each
listener's progress in step across devices. The first visit creates its admin account.

entries.name: Bazarr
entries.summary: Find and download subtitles for the films and series Sonarr and Radarr keep.
entries.description:
Bazarr looks up subtitles in the languages you want for everything in your Sonarr and Radarr libraries, and keeps them up to date.
The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: BookStack
entries.summary: A wiki organised like books: shelves, books, chapters and pages.
entries.description:
BookStack keeps documentation and notes as shelves of books, with chapters and
pages edited in a WYSIWYG or Markdown editor, and search across all of it. Sign
in first as admin@admin.com with the password password, then change both.

settings.label: Key that encrypts its sessions and secrets

Image={{ .Image }}
Environment="APP_KEY=base64:{{ .Settings.APP_KEY }}"
Environment="APP_URL=http://{{ .Name }}.local"
Environment=DB_DATABASE=bookstackapp
Environment=DB_HOST=db
Environment="DB_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=DB_USERNAME=bookstack
Volume={{ .Volumes.config }}:/config:Z

components.name: db
components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment=MYSQL_DATABASE=bookstackapp
Environment="MYSQL_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}"
Environment="MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_ROOT_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=MYSQL_USER=bookstack
Volume={{ .Volumes.mysql }}:/config:Z

entries.name: Calibre-Web
entries.summary: Browse, read and download the ebooks of your Calibre library.
entries.description:
Calibre-Web gives your Calibre library a web page: browse and search your books,
read them in the browser, send them to an ereader or download them. Point it at
the shared folder that holds your library's metadata.db. Sign in first as admin
with the password admin123, then change it.

settings.label: Run Calibre-web as this group id.
Run Calibre-web as this user id.

entries.name: Changedetection.io
entries.summary: Watch web pages and get told when they change: prices, stock, news.
entries.description:
Changedetection.io checks the pages you give it on a schedule and tells you
what changed, by email, ntfy, Gotify and many more. It has no password until
you set one in its settings.

entries.name: code-server
entries.summary: VS Code in the browser, running on your server.
entries.description:
code-server runs VS Code on the Node, so you can edit code and use a terminal
from any browser. Its password is made up at install; copy it from the
Service's settings.

settings.label: Password for sudo in its terminal

entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
Environment=DEFAULT_WORKSPACE=/config/workspace
Environment="PASSWORD={{ .Settings.PASSWORD }}"
Environment=PGID=1000
Environment=PUID=1000
Environment="SUDO_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.SUDO_PASSWORD }}"
Environment="TZ={{ .Settings.TZ }}"
Volume={{ .Volumes.config }}:/config:Z
Volume={{ .Volumes.projects }}:/projects:Z

entries.name: ConvertX
entries.summary: Converts files between formats in the browser: documents, images, audio, video and more.
entries.description:
ConvertX takes a file and gives it back in another format, with over a thousand
conversions through ffmpeg, ImageMagick, Pandoc, LibreOffice and others, all
run on the Node. Create the first account on the first visit; the first account
is the only one unless registration is allowed.

entries.name: Dashy
entries.summary: A start page for your home server, configured in one YAML file.
entries.description:
Dashy is a dashboard of your apps and links with status checks, widgets and
themes, set up in its editor or in conf.yml. It has no login until you set
one in its configuration.
entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
HealthInterval=1m30s
HealthTimeout=10s
HealthRetries=3
HealthStartPeriod=40s
Environment=NODE_ENV=production
Volume={{ .Volumes.user_data }}:/app/user-data:Z
HealthCmd=["node","/app/services/healthcheck.js"]

entries.name: Deluge
entries.summary: A BitTorrent client with a full web page: labels, plugins and per-torrent limits.
entries.description:
Deluge downloads torrents into the shared Downloads folder, with plugins for
labels, scheduling and RSS feeds. Its web page's password starts as deluge;
change it in Preferences on the first visit. Peers reach it on the Node's port
6881.
entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
Environment=DELUGE_LOGLEVEL=error
Environment="PGID={{ .Settings.PGID }}"
Environment="PUID={{ .Settings.PUID }}"
Environment="TZ={{ .Settings.TZ }}"
Volume={{ .Volumes.config }}:/config:Z
Volume={{ .Volumes.downloads }}:/downloads:z
PublishPort=6881:6881
PublishPort=6881:6881/udp

entries.name: Docmost
entries.summary: A wiki and documentation space, written together in real time, like Notion or Confluence.
entries.description:
Docmost holds pages in spaces, edited by several people at once, with comments,
diagrams, attachments and search. The first visit creates the workspace and
its owner account.

components.name: app
components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment="APP_SECRET={{ .Settings.APP_SECRET }}"
Environment="APP_URL=http://{{ .Name }}.local"
Environment="DATABASE_URL=postgresql://docmost:{{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}@db:5432/docmost?schema=public"
Environment=REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
Volume={{ .Volumes.storage }}:/app/data/storage:Z

components.name: db
components.quadlet:
[Container]

Environment=POSTGRES_DB=docmost
Environment="POSTGRES_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=POSTGRES_USER=docmost
Volume={{ .Volumes.pgdata }}:/var/lib/postgresql/data:Z

components.name: redis

entries.name: DokuWiki
entries.summary: A wiki kept in plain text files, with no database, access control and many plugins.
entries.description:
DokuWiki is a wiki that stores every page as a text file, so it needs no
database and backs up by copying its config volume. The first visit opens its
installer, which names the wiki and creates the administrator; plugins and
templates are installed from its admin page.

entries.name: draw.io
entries.summary: Draw flowcharts, network diagrams and mockups in the browser, saved to your own files.
entries.description:
draw.io (diagrams.net) is the diagram editor, served from your Node so it loads
with no outside site. Diagrams are saved to your own device or files; the
Service stores nothing and needs no account.

entries.name: Duplicati
entries.summary: Encrypted, scheduled backups of your folders to the cloud or another disk.
entries.description:
Duplicati backs up the shared folders you give it, encrypted and
deduplicated, to cloud storage, another server or the backups folder, on a
schedule. The first visit sets its password.

entries.name: Emby
entries.summary: Stream your films, series, music and photos to the Emby apps.
entries.description:
Emby organises your films, series, music and photos and streams them to its
apps on TVs, phones and browsers. The first visit creates its admin account.
Hardware transcoding with the Node's graphics card needs Emby Premiere.

grants.why: Uses the graphics card you picked to convert video for devices that cannot play it as it is, instead of the processor.
grants.without: Video is converted by the processor, more slowly.

entries.name: ESPHome
entries.summary: Write and flash firmware for ESP32 and ESP8266 boards, and see them online.
entries.description:
ESPHome turns cheap ESP32 and ESP8266 boards into sensors and switches for
Home Assistant: describe a device in YAML, build its firmware and update it
over the air. Flash a new board from the browser over USB.

grants.why: Finds your ESPHome devices on the home network by their mDNS announcements, to show which are online and update them by name. Its page is then also open on your home network at the Node's address, port 6052.
grants.without: Devices are checked by ping instead, and updated by address.

entries.name: Etherpad
entries.summary: Write a document together in real time, each author's text in their own colour.
entries.description:
Etherpad is a shared text editor: open a pad, send its link, and everyone types
in it at once, each in their own colour, with the history kept. Pads are open to
anyone who reaches the page; the admin page at /admin takes the user admin and
the password made up at install.

settings.label: Password of the admin page (user admin)

entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
HealthInterval=30s
HealthTimeout=10s
HealthRetries=3
HealthStartPeriod=30s
Environment="ADMIN_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.ADMIN_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=AUTHENTICATION_METHOD=apikey
Environment=DB_FILENAME=/opt/etherpad-lite/var/dirty.db
Environment=DB_TYPE=dirty
Environment="DEFAULT_PAD_TEXT=Welcome to Etherpad!\n\nThis pad's text is synchronised as you type, so everyone viewing this page sees the same text. Share its link to write together.\n"
Environment=REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATION=false
Environment=REQUIRE_AUTHORIZATION=false
Environment=SHOW_SETTINGS_IN_ADMIN_PAGE=true
Environment=TITLE=Etherpad
Environment=TRUST_PROXY=true
Volume={{ .Volumes.var }}:/opt/etherpad-lite/var:Z
HealthCmd=["wget","-q","-O-","http://localhost:9001/health"]

entries.name: Excalidraw
entries.summary: A whiteboard for sketching diagrams that look hand-drawn.
entries.description:
Excalidraw is a drawing board in the browser for diagrams, wireframes and
sketches with a hand-drawn look. Drawings stay in your browser and export as
PNG, SVG or files.

entries.name: File Browser
entries.summary: Browse, upload and share the files in your shared folders, from a web page.
entries.description:
File Browser shows the shared folders you give it as a file manager in the
browser: upload, download, rename, edit and share links. Sign in as admin; the
first password is printed in the Service's logs when it starts.
entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
Environment=PGID=0
Environment=PUID=0
Volume={{ .Volumes.appdata }}:/srv/app-data:z
Volume={{ .Volumes.documents }}:/srv/documents:z
Volume={{ .Volumes.downloads }}:/srv/downloads:z
Volume={{ .Volumes.gallery }}:/srv/gallery:z
Volume={{ .Volumes.media }}:/srv/media:z
Volume={{ .Volumes.db }}:/database:Z
Volume={{ .Volumes.config }}:/config:Z

entries.name: FlareSolverr
entries.summary: Gets past Cloudflare's browser checks for Prowlarr and the indexers it uses.
entries.description:
FlareSolverr is a helper for Prowlarr, Sonarr and Radarr: when an indexer sits
behind Cloudflare's checks, they send the request through FlareSolverr, which
opens the page in its own browser and passes the cookies back. It has no page of
its own to speak of; add it in Prowlarr's indexer proxies as http://flaresolverr:8191.

entries.name: Focalboard
entries.summary: Kanban boards, tables and calendars for projects, like Trello or Notion's boards.
entries.description:
Focalboard is a project board: cards with properties, shown as a kanban, a
table, a gallery or a calendar, with templates for tasks, roadmaps and meeting
notes. Register the first account on the first visit. The project is community
maintained and moves slowly.

entries.name: Forgejo
entries.summary: Host your own Git repositories, with issues, pull requests and CI.
entries.description:
Forgejo is a community-run Git forge. Keep your code and its history on your
own Nodes, review changes in pull requests, track issues, and push over
HTTPS or SSH (port 2222 on the Node).

entries.name: FreshRSS
entries.summary: Follow websites, blogs and news through their feeds, in one place.
entries.description:
FreshRSS gathers the RSS and Atom feeds you follow and lets you read them in one
list, in the browser or in any app that speaks its API. The first visit runs its
setup, where you create your account.

entries.name: Ghost
entries.summary: Publish a blog or newsletter, with members and paid subscriptions.
entries.description:
Ghost is a publishing platform for a blog, a magazine or a newsletter, with an
editor, themes, members and paid subscriptions. Create the owner account at
/ghost on the first visit.

components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment=database__client=mysql
Environment=database__connection__database=ghost
Environment=database__connection__host=db
Environment="database__connection__password={{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=database__connection__user=ghost

Environment="MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_ROOT_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=MYSQL_USER=ghost
Volume={{ .Volumes.mysql }}:/var/lib/mysql:Z

entries.name: Gitea
entries.summary: Git hosting with pull requests, issues, a package registry and CI, like a small GitHub.
entries.description:
Gitea hosts your Git repositories with code review, issues, wikis, releases, a
package registry and GitHub-compatible Actions. The first visit runs its setup
page and creates the administrator. Git over SSH is on the Node's port 222.
entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
Environment=USER_GID=1000
Environment=USER_UID=1000
Environment="GITEA__server__ROOT_URL=http://{{ .Name }}.local/"
Environment="GITEA__server__SSH_DOMAIN={{ .Name }}.local"
Environment=GITEA__server__SSH_PORT=222
Volume={{ .Volumes.data }}:/data:Z
PublishPort=222:22

entries.name: Gotify
entries.summary: Send push notifications to your phone from your own server.
entries.description:
Gotify receives messages from scripts and apps over a simple REST API and
pushes them to its Android app and the browser. Sign in as admin with the
password made up at install.

entries.name: Grafana
entries.summary: Dashboards and alerts for your metrics, logs and traces.
entries.description:
Grafana draws dashboards from Prometheus, InfluxDB, Loki, databases and many
more, and alerts you when something crosses a line. Sign in first as admin
with the password admin; it asks for a new one.

entries.name: Grocy
entries.summary: Track what is in your kitchen, what to buy, and the chores around the house.
entries.description:
Grocy keeps stock of your food and household supplies with best-before dates,
plans meals and shopping lists, and tracks chores, tasks and batteries. Sign in
first as admin with the password admin, then change it.

entries.name: Healthchecks
entries.summary: Watches your scheduled jobs: each pings it on time, and you hear when one goes quiet.
entries.description:
Healthchecks gives each backup, cron job or script a URL to ping when it has run;
when a ping is late, it alerts you by email, ntfy, Gotify, Matrix, Telegram and
many more. Sign in with the administrator's email and the password made up at
install.
entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
Environment=APPRISE_ENABLED=False
Environment=DEBUG=False
Environment=PGID=1000
Environment=PUID=1000
Environment="SECRET_KEY={{ .Settings.SECRET_KEY }}"
Environment=SITE_NAME=Healthchecks
Environment="SITE_ROOT=http://{{ .Name }}.local"
Environment="SUPERUSER_EMAIL={{ .Settings.SUPERUSER_EMAIL }}"
Environment="SUPERUSER_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.SUPERUSER_PASSWORD }}"
Environment="TZ={{ .Settings.TZ }}"
Environment=INTEGRATIONS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS=True
Volume={{ .Volumes.config }}:/config:Z

entries.name: HedgeDoc
entries.summary: Write Markdown notes together in real time, with slides, diagrams and maths.
entries.description:
HedgeDoc is a collaborative Markdown editor: everyone with a note's link edits it
at once, with live preview, slide mode, diagrams and maths. Register an account
on the first visit; notes are kept in a database in its config volume.
entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
Environment="CMD_ALLOW_ORIGIN={{ .Name }}.local"
Environment="CMD_DOMAIN={{ .Name }}.local"
Environment=CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=false
Environment=CMD_URL_ADDPORT=false
Environment="PGID={{ .Settings.PGID }}"
Environment="PUID={{ .Settings.PUID }}"
Environment="TZ={{ .Settings.TZ }}"
Volume={{ .Volumes.config }}:/config:Z

entries.name: Heimdall
entries.summary: A start page of tiles for your apps and links.
entries.description:
Heimdall is a dashboard of tiles for the apps and sites you use, some of
which show live information. Users and passwords are optional, in its
settings.

entries.name: Homarr
entries.summary: A start page for your home server, with every app and its status in one place.
entries.description:
Homarr is a dashboard: arrange tiles for your apps, bookmarks and widgets
(weather, calendars, media, downloads) and see at a glance what is up. The
first visit creates its admin account.

settings.label: Key that encrypts its stored secrets

entries.name: Home Assistant
entries.summary: Control your lights, heating, plugs and sensors from one place, without the cloud.
entries.description:
Home Assistant connects the smart devices in your home, from lights and
thermostats to plugs, sensors and speakers, and lets you control them
together and automate them, all from your own server. The first visit
creates its owner account.

Its add-on store is part of Home Assistant OS and not of this install; the
usual add-ons, such as Mosquitto and Zigbee2MQTT, are Services of their own.
Bluetooth and Zigbee or Z-Wave sticks plugged into the Node are not yet
available to it here.

grants.why: Finds the devices on your home network by listening for their announcements (Chromecast, Sonos, HomeKit, smart plugs and most local integrations), and answers HomeKit on its own ports. Its page is then also open on your home network at the Node's address, port 8123.
grants.without: Add devices by their address. Integrations that find devices by themselves, and HomeKit, will not work.

entries.name: Homepage
entries.summary: A start page for your home: links to every Service, with live status from the ones it knows.
entries.description:
Homepage is a dashboard of your Services and bookmarks, with widgets that show
what each one is doing, the weather and the time. It is set up by editing the YAML
files in its config volume.

entries.name: Immich
entries.summary: Back up and browse your photos and videos, with search by faces and things.
entries.description:
Immich keeps your photos and videos on your own Nodes. The phone apps back
them up as you take them; the web page browses them by date, place, people
and what is in them, found by its own machine learning.

components.name: server
machine-learning
redis
database
components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment=POSTGRES_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}
Environment=POSTGRES_USER=postgres
Environment=POSTGRES_DB=immich
Environment=POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS=--data-checksums
Volume={{ .Volumes.database }}:/var/lib/postgresql/data:Z
ShmSize=128m

entries.name: IT Tools
entries.summary: Handy tools for developers: encoders, converters, generators and more.
entries.description:
IT Tools is a collection of small tools in the browser: base64 and URL
encoders, hash and UUID generators, JSON and YAML converters, colour pickers and
many more. It keeps nothing and has no accounts.

entries.name: Jellyfin
entries.summary: Stream your movies, shows and music to any device.
entries.description:
Jellyfin is a free media system. Point it at your films, series, music and
photos and watch them from your TV, phone or browser.

entries.name: Jellyseerr
entries.summary: Let your household ask for films and series, and send them to Sonarr and Radarr.
entries.description:
Jellyseerr shows what is on your Jellyfin, Emby or Plex server and lets the
people who use it ask for more; approved requests go to Sonarr and Radarr. The
first visit connects it to your media server.

entries.name: Jellystat
entries.summary: Statistics for Jellyfin: what is watched, by whom, how much, and library growth.
entries.description:
Jellystat watches a Jellyfin server and keeps its playback history: the most
watched films and series, each user's activity, and how the libraries grow. On
the first visit create its account, then point it at Jellyfin by Service name,
http://jellyfin:8096, with an API key from Jellyfin's dashboard.

entries.name: Joplin Server
entries.summary: Sync your Joplin notes between devices through your own server.
entries.description:
Joplin Server keeps the notes of the Joplin apps in step across your phone,
computer and tablet, and shares notebooks. Sign in first as
admin@localhost with the password admin, then change both.

entries.name: Karakeep
entries.summary: Save links, notes, images and PDFs; it fetches a preview and tags them for you.
entries.description:
Karakeep keeps everything you want to read later in one library, fetches each
page's title and preview with its own headless Chrome, and searches the full
text. With an OpenAI key it also tags and summarises what you save. Register the
first account on the first visit; there are browser extensions and mobile apps.

settings.label: OpenAI API key, for automatic tagging (leave empty for none)

entries.name: Kavita
entries.summary: Read your comics, manga and ebooks in the browser, with your place kept.
entries.description:
Kavita serves your comics, manga and ebooks from a shared folder, with a
reader in the browser and OPDS for reading apps. The first visit creates its
admin account.

entries.name: KitchenOwl
entries.summary: A shared grocery list and recipe book for the household, with meal planning.
entries.description:
KitchenOwl is a shopping list the whole household edits at once, with recipes
that add their ingredients to it, a meal plan for the week, and expense
splitting. Create the first account on the first visit; there are mobile apps.

entries.name: Komga
entries.summary: Read your comics, manga and ebooks from a shared folder, in the browser or an app.
entries.description:
Komga serves your comics, manga, BDs and ebooks with a reader in the browser,
OPDS for reading apps, and Tachiyomi and Mihon support. The first visit creates
its admin account.

entries.name: LibreSpeed
entries.summary: Test the speed between your devices and your server, from any browser.
entries.description:
LibreSpeed measures download, upload, ping and jitter between your browser
and the Node, to check your home network and Wi-Fi.

entries.name: Lidarr
entries.summary: Follow your favourite artists and fetch their new albums.
entries.description:
Lidarr watches for new releases from the artists you follow, sends them to your download client and files them in your music folder, named and tagged.
The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: linkding
entries.summary: Save, tag and search your bookmarks, with copies of the pages kept.
entries.description:
linkding is a bookmark manager: save links from its browser extension or
bookmarklet, tag them, search them, and keep a copy of each page in case it
disappears. Sign in as admin with the password made up at install.

entries.name: Linkwarden
entries.summary: Bookmarks that keep a copy of every page, with tags, collections and full-text search.
entries.description:
Linkwarden saves a link with a screenshot, a PDF and the page's text, so it still
reads when the site is gone, and organises links into collections and tags that
can be shared. Register the first account on the first visit; it has browser
extensions and a mobile app.

components.name: app
components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment="DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:{{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}@db:5432/linkwarden"

entries.name: Memos

Markdown and found again by tag or search. The first account created is its admin.

entries.name: Minecraft Server

asks your router to forward the game port for you.

entries.name: Monica

family, the conversations you had, birthdays and other dates to be reminded of,
gifts given and planned, and a journal. Register the first account on the first
visit.

sensors publish, Home Assistant and Node-RED subscribe. Devices on your home
network reach it at the Node's address, port 1883. It runs without passwords,

entries.name: n8n
entries.summary: Automate work across your apps and services, with workflows built in the browser.
entries.description:

do something in others, with hundreds of integrations and code where you need
it. The first visit creates its owner account.

entries.name: Nextcloud
entries.summary: Content collaboration platform

Discover the ultimate solution for remote collaboration with Nextcloud. Unlike traditional office software, Nextcloud seamlessly integrates files, communication, and productivity tools into one platform, enhancing teamwork and streamlining your workflow. Say goodbye to the limitations of conventional tools and embrace a new era of collaboration.

Nextcloud stands out with its robust features tailored for every need. Enjoy secure file storage, real-time communication via Talk, comprehensive groupware, and powerful office integration, all in one place. Experience these top-notch features at an affordable price, making it accessible for everyone to elevate their collaboration game.

Deploying Nextcloud on a Zima private cloud device brings unparalleled convenience. Benefit from unlimited storage, secure data privacy, local network speeds, and multi-device access, ensuring you have everything you need at your fingertips.

entries.name: NocoDB

NocoDB is a no-code database: tables edited like a spreadsheet, with grid,
kanban, gallery, form and calendar views, links between tables, and an API for
every base. Register the first account on the first visit; it keeps its data in

entries.name: Node-RED

entries.description:
Node-RED builds automations by connecting nodes in a flow: MQTT messages,

no login until you set one in its settings file.

entries.name: ntfy

script, a backup job or Uptime Kuma, can send a message to a topic, and the ntfy

entries.name: Ollama
entries.summary: Run large language models on your own server, for Open WebUI and other apps.

and more) and answers other apps over its API, at http://ollama:11434 on the
Node's network. It runs on the processor here; larger models need plenty of
memory. Its page only says it is running: talk to it through Open WebUI.

entries.name: Open WebUI
entries.summary: A chat page for the language models you run, with Ollama or any OpenAI-style API.
entries.description:
Open WebUI is a chat interface for language models: talk to models running in
Ollama on your Node, or to any service with an OpenAI-compatible API, with
history, documents and per-person accounts. The first account created is its
admin. Install Ollama first, under the name ollama, or change the address.

entries.name: Overseerr
entries.summary: Lets your household request films and series, and sends the requests to Sonarr and Radarr.
entries.description:
Overseerr is a request page for a Plex library: people browse and ask for a film or
a series, and approved requests go to Radarr and Sonarr. Sign in with the Plex
account that owns the server, then connect Plex, Radarr and Sonarr by their
Service names.

entries.name: PairDrop
entries.summary: Send files and text between phones and computers from a web page, like AirDrop.
entries.description:
PairDrop is a page you open on two devices to send files or text straight
between them. Devices that reach it through the same Node see each other at
once; others can be paired with a six-digit code. Nothing is stored on the
Service.

entries.description: Paperless-ngx is a community-supported open-source document management system that transforms your physical documents into a searchable online archive so you can keep, well, less paper.

entries.name: PhotoPrism
entries.summary: Browse, search and organise your photos, found by place, face and subject.
entries.description:
PhotoPrism indexes the photos and videos in a folder you pick and lets you
browse them by date, place, person and what is in them, without changing the
files. Sign in as admin with the password made up at install. It needs a few
gigabytes of memory while it indexes.

entries.name: Pi-hole
entries.summary: Network-wide Ad Blocking
entries.description:
Pi-hole is a network-wide ad-blocking platform for Linux hardware, using DNS sinkhole technology to protect devices from unwanted content without requiring client-side software. Designed for home or enterprise networks, it offers efficient ad blocking and network optimization.

Core features include network-wide ad blocking and content blocking in non-browser environments. It uses DNS sinkhole to block ads, covering mobile apps and smart TVs. Caching DNS queries speeds up everyday browsing. A command-line interface ensures interoperability with reliable control options.

It provides an intuitive web interface dashboard for viewing and managing system status. An optional DHCP server function automatically protects all devices. Capable of handling high query volumes on server-grade hardware, it supports ad blocking over IPv4 and IPv6. With efficiency and versatility at the core, the platform delivers a modern network protection solution.

**Key Features:**
- Network-wide ad blocking via DNS sinkhole technology
- Blocking content in non-browser environments, including mobile apps and smart TVs
- Caching DNS queries to speed up browsing
- Command-line interface for interoperability
- Intuitive web interface dashboard for system viewing and control
- Optional DHCP server function for automatic device protection
- Ad blocking support for IPv4 and IPv6

**Learn More:**
- [Pi-hole Official Website](https://pi-hole.net/)
- [Pi-hole GitHub](https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole)

entries.name: Pinchflat
entries.summary: Downloads YouTube channels and playlists as they publish, for Plex, Jellyfin or a podcast app.
entries.description:
Pinchflat watches the YouTube channels and playlists you give it and downloads new
videos or audio with yt-dlp, named and filed for a media server, with feeds a
podcast app can follow. It is one container with no account to create.

entries.name: Planka
entries.summary: Kanban boards for a team or a household: projects, lists, cards, labels and due dates.
entries.description:
Planka is a Trello-like board: projects hold boards of lists and cards, with
members, labels, due dates, attachments and comments. Sign in with the
administrator account made at install.

entries.name: Plex
entries.summary: Stream your films, series and music to every screen, with the Plex apps.
entries.description:
Plex Media Server organises your films, series, music and photos and streams
them to the Plex apps on TVs, phones and browsers. Sign in with your Plex
account on the first visit to claim the server. Hardware transcoding with the
Node's graphics card needs Plex Pass.

settings.label: Run Plex as this group id.

grants.why: Lets the Plex apps on your TVs and phones find the server on your home network, and lets you claim it from the first visit. Its page is then also open on your home network at the Node's address, port 32400.
grants.without: Apps find the server through your Plex account only; claim it with a token from plex.tv/claim (the Claim token setting).

grants.why: Uses the graphics card you picked to convert video for devices that cannot play it as it is, instead of the processor.
grants.without: Video is converted by the processor, more slowly.

entries.name: PrivateBin
entries.summary: Paste text that is encrypted in the browser; the Service never sees what it holds.
entries.description:
PrivateBin is a pastebin: paste text or a file, choose how long it lives and
whether it burns after reading, and share the link. Everything is encrypted in
the browser with a key that lives only in the link, so the Service stores
nothing it can read. Its settings are in conf.php in the config volume.

entries.name: Prowlarr
entries.summary: Manage the indexers Sonarr and Radarr search, in one place.
entries.description:

The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: qBittorrent

entries.name: Radarr

The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: Readeck

entries.description:
Readeck saves a web page's readable content, so an article stays even when the
site changes, and lets you highlight, label and export it as an e-book. The
first visit creates your account; there are browser extensions.

entries.name: Syncthing

entries.description:

Say goodbye to traditional cloud backup limitations and embrace the future with Syncthing. Unlike conventional cloud services that often come with privacy concerns and storage restrictions, Syncthing provides a secure, real-time file synchronization solution that keeps your data exclusively in your hands. Whether you're syncing work documents or personal photos, you have complete control over where and how your files are stored and shared.

# Features That Make a Difference

Syncthing offers a seamless, user-friendly experience with powerful features designed for everyday users. Enjoy continuous file synchronization between multiple devices without any subscription fees. Experience peace of mind knowing that your data is encrypted and protected from unauthorized access. Syncthing’s open-source nature means no hidden costs, providing a truly transparent and cost-effective solution for your file management needs.

# The Power of Syncthing on Zima

Deploying Syncthing on Zima private cloud devices unlocks unparalleled convenience: enjoy unlimited storage capacity, ensure the privacy of your data, and benefit from blazing local network speeds. Transform your data management and synchronization with the perfect combination of Syncthing’s capabilities and Zima’s powerful infrastructure.

[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment=VIKUNJA_DATABASE_DATABASE=vikunja
Environment=VIKUNJA_DATABASE_HOST=db
Environment="VIKUNJA_DATABASE_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.VIKUNJA_DATABASE_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=VIKUNJA_DATABASE_TYPE=mysql
Environment=VIKUNJA_DATABASE_USER=vikunja
Environment="VIKUNJA_SERVICE_PUBLICURL=http://{{ .Name }}.local/"
Volume={{ .Volumes.files }}:/app/vikunja/files:Z

components.name: db
components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Exec='--character-set-server=utf8mb4' '--collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci'
Environment=MYSQL_DATABASE=vikunja
Environment="MYSQL_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.VIKUNJA_DATABASE_PASSWORD }}"
Environment="MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_ROOT_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=MYSQL_USER=vikunja
Volume={{ .Volumes.mysql }}:/var/lib/mysql:Z

entries.name: Wallabag
entries.summary: Save articles from the web to read later, on any device, without the clutter.
entries.description:
Wallabag saves the articles you want to read later, strips them to their
text and images, and keeps them for its apps and browser extensions. Sign in
first as wallabag with the password wallabag, then change it.
entries.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
ContainerName={{ .Name }}
Network={{ .Network }}
HealthInterval=1m0s
HealthTimeout=3s
Environment="SYMFONY__ENV__DOMAIN_NAME=http://{{ .Name }}.local"
Environment=SYMFONY__ENV__SERVER_NAME=Wallabag
Volume={{ .Volumes.data }}:/var/www/wallabag/data:Z
Volume={{ .Volumes.images }}:/var/www/wallabag/web/assets/images:Z
HealthCmd=["wget","--no-verbose","--tries=1","--spider","http://localhost/api/info"]

entries.name: Wallos
entries.summary: Keeps track of your subscriptions: what they cost, when they renew, and the total per month.
entries.description:
Wallos is a subscription tracker: enter each subscription with its price, cycle,
payment method and category, and see what the month and the year cost, with
reminders before a renewal. Create the first account on the first visit.

entries.name: Wiki.js
entries.summary: A wiki with a Markdown editor, search and per-page permissions.
entries.description:
Wiki.js keeps your notes and documentation as pages edited in Markdown or a
visual editor, with search, history and permissions. The first visit creates
its administrator account.

entries.name: WordPress
entries.summary: The web's most used site builder and blog, with its themes and plugins.
entries.description:
WordPress runs a blog or a whole site from themes and plugins, with its own
editor and accounts. The first visit asks for the site's name and its
administrator account.

components.name: app
components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment=WORDPRESS_DB_HOST=db
Environment=WORDPRESS_DB_NAME=wordpress
Environment="WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=WORDPRESS_DB_USER=wordpress
Volume={{ .Volumes.html }}:/var/www/html:Z

components.name: db
components.quadlet:
[Container]
Image={{ .Image }}
Environment=MYSQL_DATABASE=wordpress
Environment="MYSQL_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_PASSWORD }}"
Environment="MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD={{ .Settings.DB_ROOT_PASSWORD }}"
Environment=MYSQL_USER=wordpress
Volume={{ .Volumes.mysql }}:/var/lib/mysql:Z
